problem:
Let ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t)$ satisfy the homogeneous system ${x}^{′}(t)=A\text{ }x(t)$ and ${x}_{p}(t)$ satisfy the inhomogeneous system
${x}^{′}(t)=A\text{ }x(t)+f(t).$
Which of the following is **always** a solution of the same inhomogeneous system?

- ${x}_{1}(t)-4\cdot {x}_{2}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)$
- $-7\cdot {x}_{1}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)$
- $2\cdot {x}_{1}(t)+2\cdot {x}_{p}(t)$

feedback.problem: If $\,u(t)=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{4t} \\ 0\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,v(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ {e}^{2t}\end{aligned}]\,$ are solutions to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)$, find $Aw(t)$ where $w(t)=[\begin{aligned}9{e}^{4t} \\ 2{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}].$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since $u(t)$ and $v(t)$ are solutions to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ the superposition principle guarantees that 

$$
cu(t)+dv(t)
$$

 is also a solution to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)$ for all $c,d\in R.$

Notice that 

$$
w(t)=9u(t)+2v(t).
$$

 

Therefore, $w$ is a solution to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t).$ So, in order to find $Aw(t)$ we just need to find ${w}^{′}(t)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Aw & ={w}^{′}(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(9{e}^{4t})^{′} \\ (2{e}^{2t})^{′}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}36{e}^{4t} \\ 4{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
